question: Which of the following religious festivals is known as Peerla Panduga in Telangana?
solution:
The Correct answer is **Muharram**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Muharram**, also called **Peerla Panduga** is an important festival in the state of **Telangana**.
 
• Muharram is a festival marked by processions.
 
• During this occasion, a relic called **Alam** is taken out as a procession.
 
• **Ashurkhana**, representing a group of** Sufi Shrines**, is the area where the procession takes place, Many Muslims and even Hindus take part in this festival by chanting Ya Hussain as they participate eagerly in this procession.
 
• On the last day in Hyderabad, the Peerlu (Alamrelic) is carried on top of an elephant and taken in procession from Bibi ka Alam to Chaderghat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muharram:**__

 __
 
• **​**__The** first month** of the I**slamic calendar is Muharram**.
 
• The name Muharram is derived from the Arabic word **Haram**, which means **forbidden.**
 
• The Shia Muslims refer to Muharram as **Youme Ashura**.
 
• Imam Hussain and his followers were martyred in the battle of Karbala during the month of Muharram.
 
• They spend these ten days remembering martyrs.
 
• Muharram is celebrated by **Shia Muslims.**
 
 
 
• __**Christmas:**__
 __
 
• **​**__
 
 Christmas is celebrated on **December 25th** each year. 

 
 
• 
 
It commemorates the **birth of Jesus Christ** and is a central festival in Christianity.

 
 
• People decorate Christmas trees with lights, ornaments, and tinsel.
 
• Gift-giving is common, symbolizing the gifts brought by the Magi to baby Jesus.
 
• Santa Claus (or Father Christmas) brings gifts to children.
 
 
 
• __**Eid-ul-Fitr:**__
 __
 
• Eid-ul-Fitr falls on the **first day of Shawwal**, the **10th month of the Islamic calendar.**
 
• It marks the end of Ramadan, the holy month of fasting and prayer for Muslims.
 
• The greeting “**Eid Mubarak**” (meaning “Happy Eid”) is exchanged.
 
 
 
• **Navroz:**__
 
 
• **Navroz **is celebrated on the day of the astronomical vernal equinox, usually around **March 21st**.
 
• It marks the** beginning of the Persian New Year.**
 
• Families gather for a festive meal called Haft-Seen, where seven symbolic items starting with the letter “S” are displayed.
 
• Jumping over bonfires symbolizes purification and renewal.
